What a great game, this one is better than the second one.

What's in a phone? As our communications devices draw ever-nearer ourselves, so we begin to be reflected in them. Images, videos, messages, applications, and even layout all vomit a virtual breadcrumb trail that hint at who the owner is.

This is a "found-phone" story. Where is Anna? Who is Anna? What's happening? 

You'll be well-aware of what's happening a few seconds into the game, but the journey is worth it. Additionally, the audio engine ... oh man. I had to stop playing a few times, take off my headphones, and see who was at the door. The audio and spatial-positioning of the audio is very very good.

Edit: just 100% completed this game after playing for 13 hours. Well-worth the list price; I'd buy this again for the experience.

The voice acting is terrible and feels very performative, rather than being believable phone calls/voice messages. The story is linear, and there isn't much room for creativity (e.g. sending people random pictures to see how they respond), and there aren't really any things to mess around with on the phone that are interesting. The puzzles are ridiculously simple and serve no purpose other than to slow down the narrative. The jump scares, if you consider them that, are pretty pointless and don't enhance the story or experience whatsoever. The writing is generally bad and unbelievable (e.g. [spoiler]the CEO of Phresh Ideas divulging way too much information [/spoiler]), and many of the dialog options do not make sense at all. The characters frequently go between texting and calling in a way that doesn't feel believable, and behave very strangely (e.g. [spoiler]at the end of the game, a character is literally texting you as he's pushing someone to their death off of a balcony [/spoiler]). After finishing the game you can go back through more quickly to see the alternate endings, but it still takes too long, and you still have to sit through a lot of dialogue at the end at the normal speed.

Ultimately I would not recommend purchasing this game, solely because the primary focus of this game is the narrative and it felt weak. I received this game from a bundle.

So, think Orwell (if you’ve played that) and you’re sort of on the right track with this one.

It’s a game entirely contained within a fake iPhone. Not even yours. Basically, some girl called Anna’s phone ends up in your possession and you start being a real sneaky person and looking into her phone, pictures, e-mail, Twitter and all that.

It transpires, Anna is missing, as in, genuinely a missing person. All you have to go on is a video of her in a state talking about unknown forces and asking that you don't find her. You get sucked into using her phone to investigate where she could be, and ultimately what eventually happened to her. You end up meeting some of her friends and acquaintances via the phone, teaming up as you all strive to find out what has happened to Anna.

It is Live-Action acting as well, some of it is hilariously cringe (in a good, light-hearted way), and the acting isn’t top notch, but… The investigative hook, the story and the conversations within are very good. In fact, you can join in on text conversations, picking from a list of (limited) options to reply to people as you work together to find the truth.

There’s a lot of B-movie tech horror in here as well, it’s designed to be played with headphones and preferably, the lights are off! Expect lots of static, distorted voices and a low horror tone. For me, it was interesting stuff, I had a blast with it, even if I got a pretty bad ending (there are four I think).

[disclosure: I got this game for $1 as part of a Humble Bundle. I do think it's worth regular price though.]  

I enjoyed the story and felt they made good use of the mobile interface. It's basically a visual novel, so the story's on rails most of the time. However, there are points where your choices affect your relationships with the other characters, or where you know what to do (get in touch with someone) but not how to do it (you don't know her), so you need to get creative. 

Another nice thing about the game itself is the Begin+ feature, which speeds up the dialogue boxes on subsequent playthroughs. That'll get you through the game in about an hour instead of the usual three or four, making it a bit easier to try other paths and find all of the endings (I'm not there yet.) 

On the downside, I could have done without the pop scares. That's about as cheap as horror gets. Also, since the story and its dialogue options are all laid out for you, sometimes I had to say things I didn't believe or reveal information I wouldn't have revealed, and that hurts the immersion for me. Still, these are minor flaws in a fun, quick, entertaining game.

[h1]The game requires you to play a certain order. If you don't follow this order, the game breaks. Jumpscares are also not necessary[/h1]

I discovered something that relates to the person that I was supposed to reply to and it broke the game. My current "objectives" were there but I literally couldn't do it because it locked me out of a certain app in the phone and finishing the conversation was supposed to give me the "key" to the next puzzle.

How did I know? I looked up guides online and accidentally got spoiled. That's entirely my fault though, but this could've been avoided if it weren't for this game breaking bug.

I'll still continue playing the game to see if it's worthy of being "Overwhelmingly Positive", ironic because I got this in an Overwhelmingly Positive Humble Bundle and I'm giving it a negative review right now. I'll update my review if there's anything else worth saying or if I see that the story is worth changing my negative review into a positive review.

Just finished my first playthrough of this game are here are my thoughts:

Pros:
*Length was good for the price
*Story kept me invested throughout
*Some truly creepy moments that made me think about how themes in the game relate to potential problems in the real world
*A few not-so-obvious puzzles that gave me a sense of satisfaction when I figured them out

Cons:
*Most of the puzzles are pretty weak and repetitive
*There were a couple times where I was having two different conversations with the same person at the same time in the same text thread. I would say this is a glitch thought should have been remedied by now.
*Game crashed three times on me, and my system is no slouch
*The acting is pretty cringe-worthy.
*Ending was pretty unsatisfying, but I can go back and try again I guess...

In the end I think it was definitely worth a couple bucks and was a refreshing departure from the usual.

Simulacra has some similar concepts to Emily Is Away, but it's creepy rather than nostalgic. Obviously, it is way more immersive when played on smartphone, but still very atmospheric on PC.

Pros:
+ Good believable writing
+ Balances satire/comedy and horror well, progressively leaning towards the latter
+ Puzzles that require searching for data in emails and dialogues are unique and engaging

Cons:
- Really bad acting, even by FMV game standards)
- The ending is a bit disappointing, it lacks any subtlety or ambiguity that good mystery requires
